item.title: Democrat Dana LaLonde withdraws from 109th House race
item.description: Dana LaLonde announced she is stepping away from the 109th House race, saying she will stay focused on serving as a Marquette County commissioner. Anna Aho Rink will now face incumbent Rep. Karl Bohnak in November.

item.title: Michigan GOP blasts MDHHS plan allowing populous counties to compete for rural health funds
item.description: Michigan House Republicans are criticizing the state health department’s plan to distribute more than $173 million in federal rural health funding, arguing the eligibility rules could disadvantage Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula. State officials say the proposal follows federal guidelines and will prioritize areas with the greatest health care needs.

item.title: Washington’s “Potomac Phil” Predicts Additional Weeks of Winter Weather and Months of Political Gridlock
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - Celebrating Groundhog Day with Punxsutawney Phil is an event steeped in American history. Folklore claims if the groundhog sees his shadow, we’ll have six more weeks of winter. In Washington, D.C., they have their own version of Groundhog Day.

item.title: Delta Conservation District launches 2026 Tree Sale
item.description: A variety of pine trees, fruit trees, wildlife shrubs, and other plants are available to order now through April 15.

item.title: Valentine’s fundraiser supports Delta Animal Shelter through Feb. 6
item.description: For $25, donors receive Saykllly's chocolate hearts, a rose from Trotter's Floral, a valentine made by shelter staff, and a photo of an animal living at the shelter. Each animal pictured will receive a sweet treat of their own on February 14.

item.title: Government Begins Week Partially Shut Down with Debate Over ICE, DHS Funding Front and Center
item.description: The Senate passed a temporary spending bill ahead of the deadline, but that measure still needs approval in the House — where lawmakers are scrambling to tee up a vote on it this week.

item.title: NMU Beaumier Heritage Center relocates to Harden Hall
item.description: After a grand opening over the weekend, two new exhibits are on display at the new home of the Beaumier Heritage Center. This includes a year-round exhibit detailing the early years of the university, and a temporary exhibit on the dialogue and partnership of George Shiras III and Theodore Roosevelt, dubbed The Conservationists.

item.description: The person who fell through the ice today was able to get themselves out of the water and off the ice safely, a little wiser, a lot colder, and certainly lucky.
